source.section: PDF page 9, Line 26 (the United States ... including the military); Form IT-201 line 26; Form IT-201 lines 19, 24, 32-39 (PDF pages 2-3); IT-201-I PDF page 11 (line 34 standard deduction table), PDF pages 12 and 33 (line 39, rate schedule)

worked: Married filing jointly, 55 and 52. Person 0: federal civil service (CSRS/FERS annuity) pension 50,000. Person 1: military retired pay 30,000 and wages 90,000. Both pensions are from the United States, so line 26 subtracts both in full at any age. Federal AGI (IT-201 line 19) = 170,000.00. Federal taxable income = 170,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction = 138,500.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtraction: line 26 federal civil service pension (person 0) 50,000.00. Subtraction: line 26 military retired pay (person 1) 30,000.00. Line 32 total subtractions = 80,000.00. Line 33 New York AGI = 170,000.00 - 80,000.00 = 90,000.00. Line 34 New York standard deduction (married joint, PDF page 11 table) 16,050.00; line 35 = 90,000.00 - 16,050.00 = 73,950.00; line 36 dependent exemption 0 (no dependents); lines 37/38 taxable income 73,950.00. Rate schedule (PDF page 33, married joint) on 73,950.00: 17,150.00 x 4% = 686.00; 6,450.00 x 4.5% = 290.25; 4,300.00 x 5.25% = 225.75; 46,050.00 x 5.5% = 2,532.75; schedule tax = 3,734.75. NY AGI is 107,650 or less and line 38 is 65,000 or more: the rate schedule applies (PDF page 12, line 39); no recapture worksheet. Line 39 NYS tax = 3,734.75. Credits: none (the household credit, line 40, PDF page 12 tables 1-3, allows no credit above federal AGI of 28,000 single or 32,000 other statuses): state income tax = 3,734.75.
